$comment: Every public SDK method, as language-neutral data: the playground (packages/playground) builds its forms from it, the docs site's SDK explorer reads it, and other SDKs generate code snippets from it. tests/catalog.test.ts (TypeScript) checks it against the code. A resource is a client property (hc.library), except where `call` is "function": then each method is a function imported from `module` and called with the client first. Calling a method: pass `params` positionally, in order. An unset optional param is left out (trailing ones dropped). An `options` param becomes an object holding only the fields that were set (nested `options` fields the same way); a required `options` param is passed even when empty. `enum` values are written as the SDK enum's member key ("WantToRead") and passed as that member (UserBookStatus.WantToRead). `lines` is an array of `itemKind` values. `datetime` is an instant (a Date, or an ISO string). `json` is passed as parsed JSON. `nullable` means an empty value is passed as null rather than left out. Kinds: number, text, longText (multi-line), lines, date (YYYY-MM-DD), datetime, boolean, enum (`enum` names an SDK enum; optional `values` limits it to those member keys), literal (`values` are the accepted strings), options (`fields`), json, period (stats only: {kind: life|year|month|custom, year, month, from, to}, built with the stats module's `period` helpers). `example` values work against production; ids that belong to the signed-in reader (library entries, lists, goals) have no example, and their `hint` says where to get one. `scopes` copies the method's Scopes: doc line. `writes`: it changes data on the server. `destructive`: it deletes or removes something. `returns` is the TypeScript return type, for reference. `exampleFrom` (optional) is a read-only lookup that finds an example in the signed-in reader's own account: call `method` with `args` ("$me" is the reader's id, "$<input>" another input's current value, "$entry" the reader's newest library entry id) and take `pick` from the result (a dot path; `*` maps over an array). Fixed examples are production ids. When an input has both, `example` is the fallback without a signed-in reader and `exampleFrom` wins with one. An empty `pick` takes the whole result.
